title: #iloveyousomuchicoulddie #monapirnot #lucashnath #nytw #newyorktheatr...
transcript: Last night, I saw I Love You So Much I Could Die at New York Theatre Workshop, and I looooved it. It’s a new piece by Mona Pirnot, directed by Lucas Hnath. It was amazing — simple but so effective and emotional, it really resonated with me. The entire show is a collection of alternating monologues and songs, during which Mona sits at a table with her back to the audience. The monologues are written in her voice, but performed by Microsoft David, a computer-generated voice. And Mona performs the songs with her guitar. The material itself is pretty dark, as it directly references death, loss, and grief, and it's hard to explain but I think the contrast between the abrasive computer-generated voice and the emotional release of the live music is what really got me. Everything was simple, intentional but effective, even Mona sitting with her back to the audience unexpectedly created intimacy as opposed to distance. I think people will have a wide array of experiences with this piece because it's definitely not a traditional play or musical and because of the subject matter but I love to cry so I would definitely recommend it. With that, another program for my collection.
